I've added Amendment 3 to ADR-0064 and appended C.14 (BE-R3) and B.8 (DO-D4) to the work split. All the required checks exit 0. One design point needs your confirmation: the literal D-260 rule for automation rows would explain none of the rows DO-D3 measured, so Amendment 3 explains them through other recorded links.

**Checks:** `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm openapi:lint` and the repository-wide prettier check all exit 0. The DG6 historical validator printed `PASS gate DG6 (historical)` before I edited anything and exited 0 at the end. My first validator command piped through `tail`, so its echoed exit code was tail's; the end run was captured without a pipe. I didn't run `pnpm test` or any integration test, because this task only changes documents. Both documents only gained lines (264 added to the ADR, 121 to the work split, 0 deleted).

**What Amendment 3 decides:**
- **Automation rows (needs your confirmation):** the measured rows come from a built-in "starter" rule that runs as the service identity, so `initiating_user_id` is always NULL. A rule over that column alone explains nothing.
  - Instead, an execution is explained when its trigger (an outbox row) was written in the same database transaction as an audited change by a drill actor. Same transaction means the same timestamp on the same record. The rows the worker then writes for that job are explained too.
  - The initiating-user check from D-260 is kept as an extra condition.
  - This needs no schema change. I judge that D-260's escalation condition is not met, because every explained row traces back to a journalled actor's change. Please confirm this reading of "or equivalent recorded link".
- **Counters:** a new `counter` basis. A counter row may move from old to new only when the new explained coded rows in its transformation carry exactly the numbers old+1 to new. New coded rows that didn't move the counter are also reported. A prefix that hasn't been mapped is always unexplained. This needs migration `0151` (one more value in an existing CHECK), one added API enum value, and allowance format `/3`, which adds a `counters` key.
- **D8 gate chain:** D8 reads `getGate` and fixes each missing item through a fixed list of public API calls named by operation id. It then submits with `submitGate`, and a different rebound approver records a SYNTHETIC `deferred` decision with `decideGate`. An item not on the list stops D8 with an exact message. The shipped demo data is unchanged.
- **BE-R2 question 1:** a correction table fixes the counts: 15 columns compared out of 17. BE-R2's code already does this. The measured shared-baseline count of 45 is recorded against residual 1 (the ADR's reading of the migrations gave 44).

**Still open:**
- **Scheduled jobs:** automation started by a schedule has no drill actor behind it, so it stays unexplained. If one runs during the drill, T-B11 fails and you decide; DO-D4 must not pause the scheduler to avoid it.
- **G5 not measured:** the G5 fix list is written from the code and DO-D3's measured refusal, not from a run. Which adoption item the demo is missing, and whether its KPIs reach `ok`, are unknown; either can stop D8.
- **Prefix map:** I only verified the main code prefixes; BE-R3 fills in the rest.
- **Not decided:** BE-R2's question 2 (its load fixes) was outside this assignment.
- **Heading clash:** "B.8 DO-D4" repeats the existing B.8 heading number, as B.6 and B.7 did, because the assignment named it.

Nothing was committed. Merge order: AN-R1 and BE-R3 in either order, then DO-D4.
